x: Dicky Dumbrill turned up at Belgrave Hall for the opening race of the cross-country season complete with medal ribbons of the Croix de Guerre emblazoned with star and oak leaves.
Among the sprinters, Teddy Read improved by leaps and bounds as the season progressed, and was given good support by Dicky Dumbrill and Jack Frost.
Len Marchant was behind Parlett of Dorking over the half-mile stage, but Jack Frost pulled up a little, and then Dicky Dumbrill almost caught his man over the first 220.
Wickerson, the well-known sprinter, who was running for Cambridge. Jack Frost, our track Vice-Captain, was second, and Dicky Dumbrill fourth. The 220 Yards saw Jack Frost an easy winner and A.
Dicky Dumbrill also ran third in the second race over this distance. Jack Frost was second in the first 220 Yards, while Ted Read won the second-string race.

…er of competitors being limited, it was decided to merge the two contests. Dick Negus ran well in the Junior 100, while Dicky Dumbrill took second place in the Senior event, and also won the 220 Yards race.…
Freestone ran well to beat Dicky Dumbrill for premier honours with Hawkins in third place.
Dicky Dumbrill won the 100 Yards for the North with Frank Simmons second and Frank Webb third. Bob Wise won the 440 for the South, and Blowfield beat Ken Stimpson in the 1 Mile.

On Tuesday, July 23rd, we visited the Alperton Lane Track for a match with the local club, Thames Valley Harriers, and the Metropolitan Police were also present. Jack Wigley won the 100 Yards for the home club, with Dicky Dumbrill in second place, a position he also occupied in the 220.
The 100 Yards Club Championship was won by Ted Read, who beat Dicky Dumbrill with Jack Frost third, and the holder, Stan Botwright, beaten into fourth place.
Wickerson, running for Cambridge H., won the 100 Yards with George Pallett beating Dicky Dumbrill for second place.

In the 4 x 100 Yards Relay our four ran second to Achilles, our runners were Teddy Read, Dicky Dumbrill, Jack Frost and Michael Broadbent. Another Relay success was at Guildford, Lulham, Hawkins, Osmint and Read each pulled away from their rivals.
